fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Circular Driveway; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Open Lawn Area; Open Green Space; Walkway; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Circular Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Long Driveway; Limited Rear Access; Multiple Access Points
fr.recommendations:
• Install reflective address markers at both the circular driveway entrance and the access drive entrance so responders can identify the correct entry point at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Mark which driveway entry and exit points connect to the main residence versus the detached structure so responders can route correctly on arrival.
• Post a visible sign or marker at the fork between the circular driveway and access drive indicating which route leads to each structure.
• Trim vegetation along the long driveway to maintain overhead and side clearance for fire apparatus and ambulances.
• Keep the access drive free of parked vehicles so it remains passable for emergency equipment.
• Clear any vegetation or debris from the area around the detached structure so responders can move around it on foot.
• Mark the rear boundary or rear approach limitations so responders know early that rear vehicle access is restricted.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of overflow parking that would block turnaround movement on the circular driveway.
• Confirm the circular driveway can support the weight of a fire engine and repair any soft or undermined sections that could cause a heavy vehicle to become stuck.
• Identify and mark any low-clearance branches over the driveway that could obstruct tall emergency vehicles.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Shrubs; Open Green Space; Limited Vegetation Separation; Vegetation Near Structure; Multiple Access Routes; Vegetation Along Driveway; Open Clearing; Brush Area
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back all shrubs and low branches that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house walls.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open gaps between individual trees and between the trees and the house.
• Remove or cut back brush in the brush area closest to the structure.
• Clear low-hanging branches from trees near the house so flames cannot climb from ground-level vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Separate scattered shrubs near the structure so they are standing alone rather than growing in connected patches.
• Keep both driveway access routes free of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along their edges.
• Trim vegetation growing along the sides of the driveway so branches do not scrape vehicles or block passage.
• Maintain the open clearing as a vegetation-free or very low-growth area and remove any shrubs or woody plants that are beginning to establish there.
• Cut back any brush or shrubs at driveway entry points so sight lines are clear and access is unobstructed.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from shrub patches near the structure before dry season.
• Thin shrubs and small trees on the sides of the house where vegetation is growing closest to the walls.
• Keep the open green space mowed or grazed short so it does not become overgrown and connect to vegetation near the house.
